controls.label: Initial amount N0
controls.help: Sets the starting amount in mol; it scales the remaining amount N(t), while the remaining fraction f is unchanged because it divides N0 out.

controls.label: Decay constant lambda
controls.help: Sets the decay rate in 1/y; it scales the exponent lambda t and its exponential exp(-lambda t), and it fixes the half-life ln(2)/lambda.

controls.label: Time t
controls.help: Sets the evaluation time in years; it changes lambda t, exp(-lambda t), N(t) and f, and it moves t relative to the half-life ln(2)/lambda.

explorations.title: Doubling the decay constant
explorations.instruction: Predict: if lambda doubles while t stays at 1 y, what happens to the remaining fraction and to the half-life readout? Then apply the preset, which sets the decay constant lambda.
explorations.observe: The exponent lambda t doubles from 0.70 to 1.40 and the decay factor exp(-lambda t) falls from 0.497 to 0.247, so the remaining amount for N0 = 4 mol drops from 1.986 mol to 0.987 mol while the half-life readout halves from 0.990 y to 0.495 y.
explorations.why: At fixed t the exponent lambda t is proportional to lambda, so doubling lambda doubles it; exp(-lambda t) is then squared, 0.497 times 0.497 giving about 0.247, which halves the remaining amount, and the half-life ln(2)/lambda is inversely proportional to lambda so it halves as well.

explorations.title: Landing on the half-life
explorations.instruction: Predict: what fraction of the initial amount remains when the time t equals the half-life ln(2)/lambda? Then apply the preset, which sets the initial amount N0, the decay constant lambda and the time t.
explorations.observe: With lambda = 0.70 1/y the half-life readout is 0.990 y; at t = 0.99 y, very close to that half-life, the exponent lambda t is 0.693 and the remaining fraction f reads 0.500 with N(t) = 1.000 mol for N0 = 2 mol.
explorations.why: Choosing t = ln(2)/lambda makes lambda t equal ln 2, so the decay factor exp(-lambda t) is one half and the remaining amount is N0/2; the plotted half-life marker therefore sits where the curve has fallen to half its starting value.

tests.name: Zero time leaves the sample untouched
Doubled decay constant halves the half-life and squares the decay factor
Time at the half-life leaves half the amount
Large rate over a long time

invariants.name: Decay factor lies between zero and one
Remaining fraction lies between zero and one
Remaining amount never exceeds the initial amount
Exponent lambda t is nonnegative and bounded by the control limits
Half-life stays within the range set by the decay constant bounds
